note: While differential diagnosis between FBXO11-related IDDFBA and syndromes like Coffin-Siris or Koolen-de Vries is clinically relevant, literature indicates FBXO11 patients can occasionally present with fifth nail hypoplasia and pear-shaped noses.

evidence.text: A Lebanese patient with a confirmed de novo pathogenic FBXO11 variant presented with phenotypes overlapping trichorhinophalangeal syndrome, including a bulbous pear-shaped nose and small/hypoplastic nails with fifth phalanx involvement.

source.title: How many phenotypes for the FBXO11 related disease? Report on a new patient with a tricho-rhino-phalangeal like phenotype
source.quote: These features include sparse hair, sparse lateral eyebrows, a bulbous pear shaped nose, a long philtrum, thin lips, small/hypoplastic nails, pes planovalgus; bilateral cone-shaped epiphyses at the proximal 5th phalanx... whole exome sequencing was performed and a heterozygous likely pathogenic variant was identified in the FBXO11 gene

evidence.text: In a cohort of 21 patients with FBXO11-related neurodevelopmental disorder, dysmorphic features were subtle, with mild intellectual disability, facial dysmorphism, hypotonia, and behavioral dysregulation representing the core clinical spectrum.

source.title: Defining FBXO11-Related Neurodevelopmental Disorder: Clinical, Molecular and Facial Assessment of 21 Patients
source.quote: Mild intellectual disability (86%), facial dysmorphism (67%), hypotonia (62%), and behavioural dysregulation (62%) were the most prevalent features.
